# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT A KS-930 F-3 PASS WITH FINDINGS (#876, tier 1)** — `af954c691` (2026-09-06 23:13→23:31 AEST; own `--shared` clone at the LITERAL SHA with `refs/qa/base` pinned, and it CONFIRMED the trap the brief named — the source repo's local `develop` is `ff5218867`, never resolved `origin/develop`) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It proved the PR UNDERSTATES itself.** The builder showed the hole on one synthetic; the tester appended each spelling to each of the **25 real Dockerfiles** — 25/25 rc 0 FALSE CLEAN at base, 25/25 rc 1 blocked at head, with the canonical form as a blocking control. **It also honoured the fixture-shape warning and built BOTH shapes**, showing a single-write fixture reds pre-fix through the FALLBACK — a block for the wrong reason that would have produced a refutation which was an artefact of the fixture. **FINDING 1 MAJOR: the class was not swept** — `npm add`, `npm install-test`/`it`, **bare `yarn`** (its default verb IS install) and `pnpm add` are still false cleans on all 25 at HEAD; and its fix-shape is structurally better than the obvious one: enumerating verbs **fails OPEN**, so INVERT it — a package-manager invocation in a verb not on a read-only allowlist counts as a write — **fails CLOSED**, the direction the guard's own comment asks for. **FINDING 3: `pnpm i` is caught only BY ACCIDENT** (no left word boundary, so `npm[ \t]+i` matches inside `pnpm i`; control `RUN mynpm i` is newly recorded too). **FINDING 2 is a NEGATIVE RESULT and it refutes WEDNESDAY, not the builder:** the brief's claim that exit-code-only cells would have passed against the unfixed guard is false for the cells as shipped — stripping the substring argument gives byte-identical failure lines. The builder's hedge *"on some fixtures"* was exact; Wednesday's restatement dropped it. It then measured the four variants (A/B/C/D) to show where the claim IS true, and recommended the fifth cell that would give the substring a real red-proof. **It also volunteered that the fix is INERT on today's corpus** — byte-identical output on the real tree in both modes — and named that as the strongest argument for merging. Self-corrected in the open: its first blast-radius loop returned a confident zero because zsh does not word-split `$FILES`, and **the guard's own empty-corpus refusal caught it**; every figure re-derived under bash. Restores verified twice over — sha256 AND a suite re-run to 30/0 after each tamper. |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT A KS-926 CAMPAIGN — NO GO (#874, tier 2, docs-only)** — `fe5225f31` (2026-09-06 23:01→23:16 AEST; own `--shared` clone pinned to `refs/qa/head`/`refs/qa/base`, explicitly NOT `origin/develop` — it noted local `refs/heads/develop` is stale at `ff5218867`, so the brief's warning was real) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It gated a DOCUMENT the way you gate code, and found that the document does the thing it warns about.** Measurements sound where reachable — members 8, 9 and 10 all reproduced INDEPENDENTLY with controls — but the COUNTS and SCOPES are not. **F-5 MAJOR is the find and it lands outside the PR:** seat A's in-flight KS-930 F-3 fix (`af954c691`) leaves the CASE axis open — a `node_modules` write after the re-link spelled `copy` is CLEAN (rc 0) under BOTH guards, the #851 outage shape, and the guard emits the document's own phrase *"1 of 1 clean"*. Same root cause as tonight's launcher F-A. **F-2** the census's "live entry point" is undefined and is 5/15 not 3/17 (two guards already run via `npm run test:shell`), and the error makes coverage
